title: Verb たほうがいい
shortExplanation: Used to give advice or make a suggestion to someone - 'it's better if...'.
longExplanation: The たほうがいい grammar point is used to give advice or make a suggestion to someone. It can be translated as 'it's better if...', 'should', or 'it's a good idea to'. It is formed by conjugating the verb into the past tense (た-form) and adding ほうがいい.

examples.en: It's better if you go to bed early.

examples.jp: もっと勉強したほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Motto benkyou shita hou ga ii.

examples.jp: 病気の時は、薬を飲んだほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Byouki no toki wa, kusuri wo nonda hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's a good idea to take medicine when you're sick.

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲まないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo nomanai hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's better if you don't drink coffee.

examples.jp: この薬は飲まないほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Kono kusuri wa nomanai hou ga ii desu.
examples.en: It's better not to take this medicine.

examples.jp: 急いでいるときは、走らないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Isoide iru toki wa, hashiranai hou ga ii.
examples.en: When you're in a hurry, it's better not to run.

examples.jp: 彼に秘密を知られたくなければ、話さないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Kare ni himitsu o shiraretakunakereba, hanasanai hou ga ii.
examples.en: If you don't want him to know your secret, it's better not to tell him.

examples.jp: 雨の日には、外出しないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Ame no hi ni wa, gaishutsu shinai hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's better not to go out on a rainy day.

usageNote: Polarity is the only difference: Verb-た + ほうがいい advises doing it, Verb-ない + ほうがいい advises against it.
